key_idea: An edge (u,v,l) lies on some shortest a-b path iff dist(a,u)+l+dist(v,b)=dist(a,b) in one of the two orientations.
sketch: Compute all-pairs shortest paths with Floyd-Warshall (n<=100), or two Dijkstras from a and b. Let D=dist(a,b). Sum all edge lengths, then subtract every edge satisfying da[u]+l+db[v]==D or da[v]+l+db[u]==D. O(n^3 + m). Pitfall: the answer is the unpaved length, and several equally short paths must all be paved.
